title: The New York Times (David Gelles) — Eric on 'the Patagonia of Boats' and the third way for founders
summary: David Gelles — NYT climate correspondent, author of The Man Who Broke Capitalism and Dirtbag Billionaire (on Patagonia's Yvon Chouinard) — profiles Grady-White Boats owner Eddie Smith (age 83), who is turning down ~$400M in acquisition bids and instead transferring control to a perpetual purpose trust with profits flowing to a 501(c)(4) for conservation, health care, and education. After Smith's only son died of ALS in 2021, he lost confidence any buyer would preserve the company's culture (350 employees, extensive benefits, on-site health care, company chaplain). Transition guided by Natalie Reitman-White. Eric is quoted framing the move as the third option for founders beyond selling out or letting investors take the wheel.
blockquote: For decades we have taught founders they have only two options: Sell out, or let investors slowly take the wheel. These transactions show a third way is possible: an enduring company built around a long-term mission.
blockquote_source: Eric Ries, quoted in The New York Times
